name: integer_overflow
description: Unsafe unchecked arithmetic, silent truncation, or phantom overflow in Solidity integer math
question: The source file in `source` contains a Solidity `unchecked { }` block performing arithmetic on user-controlled or multi-step values without a preceding bounds check, or contains a narrowing integer cast (e.g. uint256 to uint8/uint32/uint128) or a multiplication-then-division (mulDiv-style) operation without using SafeCast or an overflow-safe mulDiv library, such that the result can silently overflow, underflow, or truncate and corrupt balances, accounting, or access-control values.
criteria: unchecked { } block containing addition/subtraction/multiplication on parameters or state derived from user input, with no prior validation guaranteeing safety
Explicit narrowing cast like uint8(x), uint32(x), uint96(x) applied to a uint256/larger value without SafeCast.toUintN or equivalent bounds check
Multiplication followed by division (a * b / c) on uint256 values without using a 512-bit-safe mulDiv implementation, risking phantom overflow
unchecked block lacking a comment or invariant proving overflow/underflow is impossible
Signed integer negation or division by -1 on a value that could equal type(intN).min without a guard
Accumulator variable incremented every call inside unchecked without any cap or overflow analysis
